thought.text: The pkill matched my own shell. Let me be more careful with process matching:

reasoning_content: pkill may have killed the shell itself (exit 143 = SIGTERM). Because the pattern "process-compose up" matched... hmm, actually the pkill -f pattern "process-compose up" could match the command line of my own shell. Because the shell's command contains that string. Let me be careful: use a pattern that doesn't match my own command. Check the state and get the help.

action.command: ps aux | grep -F "process-compose" | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2, $11, $12, $13}'; echo "---"; process-compose up --help 2>&1 | head -50
